latest_release.name: v2.5.0
latest_release.body:
## Security fixes

v2.5.0 fixes eight vulnerabilities in three servers. Upgrade `mcp-server-git` to 2026.11.18,
`@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` to 2.4.0 and `@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything` to 2.3.1.

| Package | Affected | Fixed in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mcp-server-git` | through 2026.11.11 | 2026.11.18 |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` | all versions before 2.4.0, and date versions 2025.1.14 through 2026.8.31 | 2.4.0 |
| `@modelcontextprotocol/server-everything` | through 2.3.0 | 2.3.1 |

### `mcp-server-git` 2026.11.18

* **A merge no longer starts Git's automatic maintenance.** A successful `git_merge`, a fast-forward included, ended in `git maintenance run --auto`, whose garbage collection runs the commands a repository's own `gc.recentObjectsHook` names, with the server's privileges. `maintenance.auto` is now `false` and `gc.auto` is `0` for every Git command the server runs ([GHSA-h2g3-rwxm-xfm3](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/security/advisories/GHSA-h2g3-rwxm-xfm3))
* **Git never fetches a missing object by itself.** A repository's configuration could declare a promisor remote and name the program Git runs to fetch from it (`remote.<name>.uploadpack`, `core.sshCommand`), which a read-only tool then started when it needed an object that was not on disk. Lazy fetching is turned off (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`), and a Git too old to honor that refuses a repository that declares a promisor remote ([GHSA-87qg-cmw8-jc5m](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/security/advisories/GHSA-87qg-cmw8-jc5m))
* **Drivers are read again after a tool writes the working tree.** A repository's configuration can include a file that a merge or checkout creates, so a filter or merge driver could appear after the server had emptied the ones it found, and run during the `git merge --abort` that follows a conflict. `git_checkout`, `git_merge` and that abort now read the drivers again before any other Git command runs. **The `--repository` confinement check is not yet repeated after such a write** (#5599) ([GHSA-9vjp-x34c-xg6v](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/security/advisories/GHSA-9vjp-x34c-xg6v))
* **A filter or merge driver with an empty name is emptied too.** Git accepts `[filter ""]`, selected by `filter=` in `.gitattributes`, and the server's list of a repository's drivers missed it, so its command ran ([GHSA-pm7p-vphh-2cg7](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/security/advisories/GHSA-pm7p-vphh-2cg7))
* **Index entries that point outside the working tree are refused.** With `--repository`, a crafted `.git/index` naming a path such as `../outside/secret` made `git_diff_unstaged` and `git_diff` return that file's content, and `git_status` report whether it exists. The index is now checked from its top before any tool reads it, and the untracked cache, which can name a directory outside the working tree, is turned off ([GHSA-r2q8-f657-4r56](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/security/advisories/GHSA-r2q8-f657-4r56))
* **A submodule's own configuration no longer runs programs.** With `diff.submodule=diff` in the repository's configuration, `git_diff` ran a nested diff inside each changed submodule under the submodule's own `diff.external` and textconv drivers, and `git_checkout` and `git_add` ran Git inside a submodule under its own configuration too. `diff.submodule` is now `short`, the drivers a checked-out submodule defines are overridden, and a Git older than 2.33, which would not pass the overrides into a submodule, is refused for a repository that has one checked out ([GHSA-8wv7-r664-7594](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/security/advisories/GHSA-8wv7-r664-7594))

### `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` 2.4.0

* **Directory listings stay with the directory that was checked** (Linux and macOS). `list_directory`, `list_directory_with_sizes`, `directory_tree` and `search_files` now list a directory in place after checking

hot_issues.title: memory: README does not say that unreadable lines are skipped, kept on every write, and fixable only by hand
git: 21 of 32 tool input properties have no description
everything: add tests that error paths carry no credential values (validation errors, gzip refusal, opt-in on or off)
memory: add tests for the graph file path being a symlink (reads follow it; a write replaces the link, not its target)
git: git_branch leaks CLI '* ' prefix, breaking downstream git_checkout / git_diff / git_show / git_merge
`interface-diff` discards the git error when resolving its default base and reports the wrong cause
memory: two processes clearing one crash-left lock guard can remove a live guard
Docker: five images ignore docker stop and are killed at the timeout

detail.readme:
# Model Context Protocol servers

This repository is a collection of *reference implementations* for the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) (MCP), as well as references to community-built servers and additional resources.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> If you are looking for a list of MCP servers, you can browse published servers on [the MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/). The repository served by this README is dedicated to housing just the small number of reference servers maintained by the MCP steering group.

> [!WARNING]
> The servers in this repository are intended as **reference implementations** to demonstrate MCP features and SDK usage. They are meant to serve as educational examples for developers building their own MCP servers, not as production-ready solutions. Developers should evaluate their own security requirements and implement appropriate safeguards based on their specific threat model and use case.

The servers in this repository showcase the versatility and extensibility of MCP, demonstrating how it can be used to give Large Language Models (LLMs) secure, controlled access to tools and data sources.
Typically, each MCP server is implemented with an MCP SDK:

- [C# MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/csharp-sdk)
- [Go MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk)
- [Java MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/java-sdk)
- [Kotlin MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/kotlin-sdk)
- [PHP MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/php-sdk)
- [Python MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk)
- [Ruby MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ruby-sdk)
- [Rust MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk)
- [Swift MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/swift-sdk)
- [TypeScript MCP SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk)

## 🌟 Reference Servers

These servers aim to demonstrate MCP features and the official SDKs.

- **[Everything](src/everything)** - Reference / test server with prompts, resources, and tools.
- **[Fetch](src/fetch)** - Web content fetching and conversion for efficient LLM usage.
- **[Filesystem](src/filesystem)** - Secure file operations with configurable access controls.
- **[Git](src/git)** - Tools to read, search, and manipulate Git repositories.
- **[Memory](src/memory)** - Knowledge graph-based persistent memory system.
- **[Sequential Thinking](src/sequentialthinking)** - Dynamic and reflective problem-solving through thought sequences.
- **[Time](src/time)** - Time and timezone conversion capabilities.

### Archived

The following reference servers are now archived and can be found at [servers-archived](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived).

- **[AWS KB Retrieval](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived/tree/main/src/aws-kb-retrieval-server)** - Retrieval from AWS Knowledge Base using Bedrock Agent Runtime.
- **[Brave Search](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived/tree/main/src/brave-search)** - Web and local search using Brave's Search API. Has been replaced by the [official server](https://github.com/brave/brave-search-mcp-server) ([`@brave/brave-search-mcp-server`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@brave/brave-search-mcp-server)).
- **[EverArt](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived/tree/main/src/everart)** - AI image generation using various models.
- **[GitHub](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived/tree/main/src/github)** - Repository management, file operations, and GitHub API integration.
- **[GitLab](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived/tree/main/src/gitlab)** - GitLab API, enabling project management.
- **[Google Drive](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived/tree/main/src/gdrive)** - File access and search capabilities for Google Drive.
- **[Google Maps](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived/tree/main/src/google-maps)** - Location services, directions, and place details.
- **[PostgreSQL](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived/tree/main/src/postgres)** - Read-only database access with schema inspection.
- **[Puppeteer](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived/tree/main/src/puppeteer)** - Browser automation and web scraping.
- **[Redis](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived/tree/main/src/redis)** - Interact with Redis key-value stores.
- **[Sentry](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived/tree/main/src/sentry)** - Retrieving and analyzing issues from Sentry.io.
- **[Slack](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived/tree/main/src/slack)** - Channel management and messaging capabilities. Now maintained by [Zencoder](https://github.com/zencoderai/slack-mcp-server)
- **[SQLite](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived/tree/main/src/sqlite)** - Database interaction and business intelligence capabilities.

## 🚀 Getting Started

### Using MCP Servers in this Repository
TypeScript-based servers in this repository can be started with `npx`.

For example, this will start the [Memory](src/memory) server:
```sh
npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory
```

Python-based servers in this repository can be started with [`uvx`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/tools/) or [`pip`](https://pypi.org/project/pip/). `uvx` is recommended for ease of use and setup.

For example, this will start the [Git](src/git) server:
```sh
# With uvx
uvx mcp-server-git

# With pip
pip install mcp-server-git
python -m mcp_server_git
```

Follow [these](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) instructions to install `uv` / `uvx` and [these](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/installation/) to install `pip`.

### Using an MCP Client
However, running a server on its own isn't very useful, and should instead be configured into an MCP client. For example, here's the Claude Desktop configuration to use the above server:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "memory": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory"]
    }
  }
}
```

On Windows, wrap `npx` with `cmd /c`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "memory": {
      "command": "cmd",
      "args": ["/c", "npx", "-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory"]
    }
  }
}
```

Additional examples of using the Claude Desktop as an MCP client might look like:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "filesystem": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/path/to/allowed/files"]
    },
    "git": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["mcp-server-git", "--repository", "path/to/git/repo"]
    },
    "fetch": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["mcp-server-fetch"]
    }
  }
}
```

On Windows, apply the same wrapper to the `npx`-based `filesystem` entry above by changing its `"command"` to `"cmd"` and prepending `"/c", "npx"` to its existing `args`. Leave the `uvx` entries unchanged.

### Transports: stdio and Streamable HTTP

An MCP server talks to its client over a **transport**. The protocol defines two standard ones, and they run very differently:

| Transport | How the server runs | How a client reaches it |
|---|---|---|
| **stdio** | The client launches the server as a subprocess and talks to it over the process's stdin and stdout. The server opens no port. | A `command` and `args` in the client's configuration, as in the examples above |
| **Streamable HTTP** | The server runs on its own as an HTTP service, and can serve many clients | A URL, such as `http://localhost:3001/mcp` |

**Every server in this repository serves stdio by default, and every one can also serve Streamable HTTP** on `http://127.0.0.1:3001/mcp` (set `PORT` and `HOST` to move it): [Everything](src/everything) with its `streamableHttp` argument (its README also covers its deprecated HTTP+SSE transport), and the others with `--transport streamable-http`, as each server's README shows. Started without one, a server uses stdio, so when you run `uvx mcp-server-git` or `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory` in a terminal, it opens no port, prints at most a one-line startup notice, and then appears to hang. That is expected: it is waiting for a client to send it messages on stdin. You do not normally start a stdio server yourself; your MCP client starts it from its configuration and stops it when it is done.

To try a server without setting up a client, use the [MCP Inspector](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector). Given a stdio server's command, it launches the server for you and lets you browse and call its tools; given a URL, it connects to a running Streamable HTTP server:

```sh
# A stdio server: the Inspector launches it
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector uvx mcp-server-git

# A Streamable HTTP server: start it first, then connect to its URL
npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything streamableHttp   # or: uvx mcp-server-time --transport streamable-http
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector --transport http --server-url http://localhost:3001/mcp
```

For more, see the [transport layer](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/learn/architecture#transport-layer) in the MCP architecture overview, and [Transports](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports) in the specification.

## 🛠️ Creating Your Own Server

Interested in creating your own MCP server? Visit the official documentation at [modelcontextprotocol.io](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction) for comprehensive guides, best practices, and technical details on implementing MCP servers.

## 📚 Learn More

See [ADDITIONAL.md](ADDITIONAL.md) for a curated list of frameworks and resources that simplify building MCP servers and clients.

## 🤝 Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for information about contributing to this repository.

## 📦 Releasing

See [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md) for how packages are published (OIDC trusted publishing from CI — no registry tokens) and how to retry a failed publish.

## 🔒 Security

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for reporting security vulnerabilities.
